sources.entry: Characterizing the Branch Misprediction Penalty - Defines the penalty as pipeline refill plus window drain, so it exceeds pipeline depth and is not constant.

summary.title: Characterizing the Branch Misprediction Penalty
summary.one_liner: Branch misprediction penalty is window drain time plus pipeline refill time, so it can be several times the front-end pipeline length and varies with program behavior.
takeaways: The branch misprediction penalty is roughly the window drain time plus the front-end pipeline refill time, so it can exceed the pipeline length.
Penalty depends on the number of instructions since the last miss event; bursts of mispredictions have shorter penalties than isolated ones.
Average critical dependence path and ILP affect drain time, which increases the penalty for low-ILP programs.
Interval analysis divides execution into intervals between miss events and is used to isolate mispredicted-branch behavior.
Measured on SPEC CPU2000 integer benchmarks in a SimpleScalar model with a 5-stage front end and 64-entry ROB.
summary.summary: The paper studies why the branch misprediction penalty in superscalar processors is often much larger than the front-end pipeline length. It identifies five contributors: front-end pipeline length, instructions since the last miss event, inherent ILP, functional unit latencies, and short L1 data cache misses. It uses interval analysis, which models performance as a sequence of intervals between miss events, and validates the analysis with simulations of SPEC CPU2000 integer benchmarks on a modeled 4-wide processor with a 64-entry ROB and a 5-stage front end. It also examines interactions with I-cache misses and long D-cache misses.
